fields.title: Forecast discussion: CME expected to arrive late on 6 November

sections.heading: Solar activity
sections.text: Region 4291 produced an X2.1 flare at 0918 UTC with an associated full halo coronal mass ejection (CME).

sections.heading: Model estimate
sections.text: Model runs place the leading edge at Earth about 30 hours after the eruption. The estimate is uncertain by several hours in either direction.

sections.heading: Expected conditions
sections.text: Geomagnetic activity should reach the G3 level shortly after the shock arrives. The strength depends on the orientation of the magnetic field inside the CME, which is not known until it reaches the upstream monitor.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.text: A rise in solar wind speed and density at the upstream monitor will give about 30 to 60 minutes notice of arrival.

fields.nextIssuance: The next discussion will be issued by 2026 Nov 05 1800 UTC.
fields.footer: Exercise product. Not an official NOAA discussion.
